overall: The AG found the Somerset Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to announce that the September 10 and 17 meetings were recorded and by failing to roll-call vote before a second executive session on September 17. The Board had already acknowledged the violations and adopted fixes, so the AG resolved the matter by informal action with a compliance order.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair did not announce at the start of the September 10 meeting that it was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges that the September 10 and 17 meetings were recorded and that the Chair neglected to make the required announcement; therefore, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair did not announce at the start of the September 17 meeting that it was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: The requirement that the chair inform attendees of any recording includes any recording made by members of the public body itself, including those made for public broadcasting or administrative purposes, such as assisting in the drafting of meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not vote by roll call the second time it entered executive session during the September 17 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges that it did not vote by roll call when it convened in executive session for a second time during its September 17 meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (recording announcements and roll-call votes before executive session).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
